classification.difficultyReason: Differentiate a supplied rational cost function, classify its stationary point and interpret the minimum on a positive domain.

content.prompt:
The cost, $C(v)$ in dollars, of a 100 km yacht journey depends on the speed $v$ of the boat in km/h.

The cost formula is given by:
$$C(v)=\frac{50000}{v}+4000+500v$$
where $v>0$.

Find the speed of the boat that will minimise the cost, and the minimum cost.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}C'(v)&=-\frac{50000}{v^2}+500\\0&=-\frac{50000}{v^2}+500\\500v^2&=50000\\v^2&=100\\v&=10\qquad(v>0).\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}C''(v)&=\frac{100000}{v^3}\\C''(10)&=100>0.\end{align*}$$
Since $C''(v)>0$ for all $v>0$, this is the global minimum. The cost is undefined at $v=0$ and grows without bound as $v$ approaches zero from above or increases without bound.
$$\begin{align*}C(10)&=\frac{50000}{10}+4000+500(10)\\C(10)&=14000.\end{align*}$$
The speed is $10\ \mathrm{km/h}$ and the minimum cost is $\$14000$.
